A NOTE ON INTERPRETATION

What Am I Actually Looking At?

Each point represents a computational state. Each coordinate represents an observable condition. Lines represent defined relationships between states. Colors represent policy or enforcement outcomes.

The three-dimensional arrangement is a projection of a higher-dimensional discrete structure. Spatial proximity in the rendering may not correspond to semantic similarity.

  1. Original computational state — the operation, environment and trace supplied by an experiment.
  2. Mathematical representation — the Boolean vector encoding selected observable conditions. It is not the complete computational state.
  3. Projection into R³ — three axes, three principal components, or a graph layout.
  4. Rendering coordinates — normalized display positions, with optional collision offsets and animation. These do not change the vector or results.

A visually connected cluster need not be connected in the original graph. A smooth-looking face does not establish continuity. A visible hole does not establish a topological hole. Graph layout distances are not semantic distances.

Local-view agreement does not establish global semantic correctness. Views are supplied memberships, not a security boundary: any state loaded into this browser is available to its user.

The default dataset is entirely synthetic. No commands were executed. It demonstrates deliberately flawed teaching rules, not measured behavior or the paper’s results.
